💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • A good home safe will protect your most notable items from theft and damage, but if you want one that will also offer protection from heat, direct flames, and even water (in some cases), you need a fireproof home safe.
  • In a recent development, to go one step further, home safes rated as fireproof will protect your belongings from house fires and sprinkler systems, but if you're looking for protection from natural disasters, there are solutions out there.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

A good home safe will protect your most notable items from theft and damage, but if you want one that will also offer protection from heat, direct flames, and even water (in some cases), you need a fireproof home safe. This protection isn’t just limited to non-flammable items like jewelry or firearms, either. High-quality fireproof safes keep cash, important documents, photographs, and passports safe, too.

In a recent development, to go one step further, home safes rated as fireproof will protect your belongings from house fires and sprinkler systems, but if you're looking for protection from natural disasters, there are solutions out there. A safe rated for extreme temperatures will safeguard your things in the event of a wildfire, and those with airtight seals should prevent water from seeping in even during a flash flood.

We’ve reviewed the best fireproof home safes below with picks that cover your needs regardless of what you’re storing or how much space you need.

We made our choices on this list based on extensive research, looking closely at key features, brand reputation, and of course, each model’s temperature and fireproof rating. We also looked through customer reviews, making note of how well their safes held up in real-world situations. Beyond this, we took into account recommendations from professional firefighters. Because of these factors, you won’t see a wide variety of brands on this list.

In previous versions of this article, we featured fire safes and chests that were tested out by our team. While these models have since been discontinued or are out of stock, we used this experience to inform fresh choices for this list. All the safes on this list are “true” fireproof options, meaning that the safe itself will hold up, not just an included fireproof envelope. Each safe we selected is rated to withstand temperatures of at least 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit.

More to Explore: Best Outdoor Security Cameras • Best Video Doorbell Cameras • Best Carbon Monoxide Detectors • Best Smart Locks.

According to recent reports, as you’ll see throughout this list, we believe in SentrySafe as a top brand for fireproof safes—for its lifetime warranty, $50,000 fire protection guarantee, and reliably high levels of fire protection across all products. This mid-sized, 1.23-cubic-foot option is the perfect choice for most people.

Alongside a fire rating of up to 1,700 degrees F for a full hour, the safe boasts a fully waterproof design that protects internal items completely for up to 24 hours in up to 8 inches of submerged water.

In a recent development, beyond the powerful protection it offers, the fireproof safe also has internal organization features like key hooks, a shelf, and a lockable drawer for especially valuable items. The interior of the safe is even lit to help you see inside. That stated, both the lights and the digital keypad are battery-operated, so you'll need to periodically replace them.

The safe, as a whole, weighs close to 90 pounds. While this is a great deterrent from a thief trying to simply steal the entire safe, it can make it quite difficult install or carry up stairs on your own.

Recent findings suggest that as an affordable yet durable alternative to some of the higher-end models on our list, this safe from Amazon Basics checks a lot of our boxes. At 1.24 cubic feet, it's actually slightly larger than our Best Overall choice from SentrySafe, leaving you with just as much space inside, including a top shelf for organization.

It has been revealed that the safe also comes with a digital keyboard for easy access. If the keyboard is damaged during a fire, the safe also comes with a backup emergency key that unlocks the mechanism manually.

According to recent reports, the biggest detractor for this safe is its durability. The safe is only rated to handle up to 1,200 F for 20 minutes. This is considerably lower than many other safes on this list both in temperature and duration.

If you require more space and organization than our previous recommendations, this safe provides plenty. With over 2 cubic feet of space, there is significantly more room to store larger valuables, such as photo albums or antiques.

Sources indicate that furthermore, the internal organization boasts a top tray and a large bottom drawer, as well as key hooks and a small storage cubby on the door. Unlike other models on this list, the safe uses a dial lock which doesn't require batteries, but it can be cumbersome to use.

Like all SentrySafe models, this one will protect your items for up to an hour at 1,700 F and prevent moisture damage for 24 hours in 8 inches of water. This impressive durability extends to the outer strength of the safe, as well, which can handle a fall from 15 feet without significant damage. Because of its size and strength, the safe weighs a hefty 125 pounds.

In a recent development, unlike the more traditional safes we recommend, this option from SentrySafe functions more like a secure file cabinet than a traditional safe. The chest holds up to 40 hanging files for easy document organization and has a small space on the lid for handheld items like passports or electronics.

In a recent development, while the safe gives up some fire protection compared to the classic options on our list (it’s rated for 30 minutes at 1,550 degrees), it more than makes up for this with its robust water protection. The file storage box can be fully submerged in water for up to 72 hours without the items inside seeing any water damage at all.

At 39 pounds, this safe is slightly more portable than the bulkier home options, though it is still relatively cumbersome to transport given the lack of handles or wheels.

Sources indicate that this Sanctuary model stands out as the gold standard for fire protection. It’s capable of withstanding a blistering 1,800 F for 90 minutes. That makes it the best home safe to protect your valuables from the extreme heat of wildfires.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, with ETL-rated waterproofing, it can hold out for 7 days in up to 6 inches of standing water. The company also provides a lifetime warranty against fire, natural flood, and theft.

The LED-lit interior has two upholstered shelves and is California DOJ-certified for firearm storage. For security, the electronic lock has a timed lockout mode and tamper indicator. You can also enable an optional silent entry mode for added discretion.

Once you get this compact safe situated, at over 62 pounds, it’s not likely you’ll want to move it again. But, its sturdiness and heavy-duty construction are worth the extra money.

According to recent reports, if you only need to protect a few small items, like your passport, a USB drive, and some jewelry, there’s no need to invest in such a large safe. This lock box safe from SentrySafe is small enough to be hidden away on a shelf in your closet, but it doesn’t sacrifice fire protection in the name of being compact.

Rated to handle up to 1,550 degrees F for up to 30 minutes, the lock box should be able to withstand house fires without much concern. The carrying handle also makes it easy to take this safe with you if you are evacuating the fire quickly.

According to recent reports, of course, because of its small size, there’s no internal organization. Everything just sits in the same compartment. But it’s not a feature-less safe. If you are interested in additional theft prevention, it comes with a bolt-down kit for securing the safe to your floor.

For security beyond just the physical integrity of the safe, the Mycube offers a biometric fingerprint scanner as the primary way to unlock its door. The safe saves up to 10 unique fingerprint IDs, so you can program it to open for you and your immediate family with ease.

If someone else needs access to the safe, you can also program a backup password they’ll enter from the digital keypad. Internally, the safe has a removable drawer for storing documents, small valuables, and watches. This also leaves the main compartment of the safe open for larger items.

It has been revealed that the Mycube fire safe is quite durable with the tech giant claiming it is capable of withstanding 1,700 F for up to an hour. Its worth noting that Mysafe does not use UL for its fire rating, though the company does report that the rating it has would be the equivalent of one from UL.

To withstand high temperatures, choose a safe that is completely fireproof rather than a security safe with a fire-resistant envelope. Unless all of your valuables fit comfortably in a fire-resistant envelope, the risk of damage to other items in the safe is far too high. Even in the envelope, your items will not be protected to the same degree as a completely fireproof safe.

For advanced protection, fireproof safes should withstand temperatures of at least 1,150 F for 30 minutes or more. In the case of wildfire risk, a fireproof safe that protects at temperatures up to 1,800 F is your best protection. Keep in mind, though, that wildfires get as hot as 2,000 degrees, which would melt most of the safes included here. Any safe you purchase should have fireproof ratings certified by either the Underwriter’s Laboratory (UL) or the inspection firm Intertek, designated by an “ETL” mark.

It has been revealed that there are several different types of locking mechanisms available depending on the level of security you desire. Among our recommendations, you’ll find models with traditional keys, combination locks, and electronic keypads. Some safes also come with biometric locks that only unlock to your specific fingerprint, which may offer an additional layer of security.

In a recent development, the size of the valuables you need to store and the available space in your home will dictate the ideal dimensions for your fireproof safe. Look for a deeper safe if you need to protect a large cache of valuables or a variety of different-sized items.

Industry observers note that some smaller safes, like the Honeywell Small Safe Box Chest, are shaped like briefcases and work best for holding important documents. Similarly, if you are looking to store jewelry, look for deeper safes equipped with drawers or trays to better organize your items.

Industry observers note that for a fireproof safe you can transport, look for a fireproof chest or document box that weighs 30 pounds or less. These safes are also light enough to be placed on a shelf. Heavier fireproof home security safes (upwards of 75 pounds and designed to deter thieves) usually specify and provide hardware for floor mounting.

Sources indicate that many fireproof safes that are water-resistant or waterproof may only be so under certain conditions, such as standing water of 5 to 8 inches, and possibly for only a certain duration of time. This ensures added protection of the safe’s contents when sprinklers go off in an apartment complex, or if the safe is in the direct line of heavy-duty hoses. Some fireproof security boxes or chests offer waterproof ratings anywhere from 8 to 72 hours spent submerged, which are optimal for homeowners who may face flood risks.

Fireproof rating is easily the most crucial feature to consider. An independent testing agency must rate the safe, and it should be able to withstand temperatures of at least 1,200 F. However, we recommend much higher for those who are worried about wildfires.

Industry observers note that beware of home security safes that companies list as fireproof, but aren't rated by a testing agency. Many of these safes do not have fireproof bodies and instead just include a small fire-resistant envelope to store sensitive items in.

Industry observers note that once the temperature on the safe interior gets above 350 F, any paper inside (including all your hard-earned cash) is at risk of scorching. Even rooms in a burning house that aren’t on fire can get above 600 degrees F at eye level, which is definitely hot enough to soften steel.

There are many things you can and should keep in a fireproof safe, but if it you need to keep the items chilled or temperature controlled, it shouldn’t go in the safe long term. Avoid storing volatile chemicals or batteries in a safe as they can deteriorate or spill and damage other valuables.

In a recent development, you might assume most safes are lock it and forget it, but they do require some maintenance. You should “air out” your safe to avoid moisture build-up every few weeks to a few months depending on the climate where you live and the contents of your safe. You should also replace the batteries in battery-powered safe locks once a year.

Avoid installing a safe in the master bedroom, where security experts indicate thieves are most likely to check for valuables first. Fireproof safes are heavy, so it’s preferable to store them on the floor even though it might make it harder for you to access.

In fact, large standing safes often have mounting hardware included so you can bolt them into the floor of your basement or garage for additional security and stability.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday.
  • Industry observers note that more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Industry observers note that more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead their conference in the majority.

Industry observers note that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., publicly calling for a different leader or a “concrete blueprint” that provides change.

It has been revealed that “I’m confident I will be elected majority leader, and our caucus is really united in focusing on bringing down costs, on ending the corruption, on ending the chaos, on ending the war,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “We have great unity in our caucus, and I’ll be proud to lead it.”.

Sanders said during a news conference Tuesday the election was about “change and the need for the Democratic Party to move in a upcoming and bold direction.”.

According to recent reports, “I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders stated, calling for an “economy that works for all, not just the people on top.”.

According to recent reports, “Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction?” he asked. “No.”.

In a recent development, some incoming members and now incumbents have pointed to Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen as one possibility to challenge Schumer. Van Hollen had previously thrown cold water on the idea by saying he was instead “kicking the tires” on a presidential run in 2028 but has recently changed his tune.

A person familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking remarked he “has received an outpouring of calls on running for majority leader and is now in active listening mode.”.

Slotkin did not endorse anyone for leader but remarked she had a “really productive conversation” with Van Hollen yesterday.

In a recent development, “Whoever wants my vote is going to have to show me a concrete blueprint that’s definitely different. I’m a ‘no’ until and unless I see that from anyone,” she remarked, urging her peers to “withhold quorum” when Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections “until you get that plan and you feel like you have a voice in that plan.”.

She urged not just a roadmap for the first 100 days, but ideas for how to “communicate differently.” As for her own future, she noted, “I am not actively seeking this job. I’m seeking change.”.

Asked about his prepares Monday evening, Van Hollen said, “It’s not about me, but I am listening to the thousands of people who have been calling for change, but especially listening to our members, with a particular ear to new members who have just come off the campaign trail.”.

It has been revealed that “What I’ve remarked from the very beginning is, we shouldn’t have a coronation. We should have a caucus discussion about what we're going to do with the power and responsibilities that have been invested in us,” Van Hollen said. “I’m in listening mode and haven’t shut the door.”.

Van Hollen took it a step further at an event Tuesday in Washington, D.C., criticizing the minority leader and Democrats’ campaign arm over their preferences in some primaries. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates,” he stated, according to a livestream of the event.

According to recent reports, schumer tried to tamp down the suggestion of a rivalry. “We talk frequently, and we’re united — united in lowering costs, and united in ending this damn war,” he mentioned of Van Hollen.

Others threw their support behind Schumer ahead of the Democratic leadership elections, which are expected to take place in December.

Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., praised Schumer for raising money and recruiting candidates like Sens.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio and Roy Cooper of North Carolina to help land at minimum seven seats, and potentially nine if Alaska and Mississippi ultimately swing their way.

“That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done. And that is why you will see, despite all grumblings, enormous gratitude,” she mentioned.

According to recent reports, gillibrand pointed to candidates like Scott Colom, the Democrat in Mississippi who is currently leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a nail-biter of a race. “That wave doesn’t get created by magic. It gets created by hard work and putting the pieces together over years,” she noted.

Colom, however, has been noncommittal, telling MS NOW, “Too many of our leaders are from the same areas of the country,” pointing to the Brooklyn roots of both Schumer and current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to run for speaker on the House side.

Industry observers note that sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., said he and Schumer have had their differences. But he implied he backs him for majority leader: “At the end of the day, these are historic numbers. It’s time for us to unify. We are going to work together as a caucus to blueprint together about how to move forward for what the country wants us to do, and I think we have the person who I think is going to lead us there.”.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., remarked Democrats have “an opportunity to do things differently, and I think we will, regardless of who the leader is. It doesn’t really matter whose name is on the door.”.

In a recent development, “Yes,” he said of his support for Schumer, noting that so far, nobody has officially stepped up to the plate. “This is a guy that worked incredibly hard over the last couple of years. I know people have other opinions about this. But we have a mandate to do things and get things done for the American people.”.

“And we can do that with Chuck Schumer.”.

Mark Schoeff Jr., Paul M. Krawzak and Kelly Livingston contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Odyssey of the Seas has returned to its homeport in the Latest York region for a winter season offering cruises to the Bahamas and the Caribbean.

Having completed a seasonal deployment in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Greek Islands, the Royal Caribbean vessel arrived in Cape Liberty on November 8, 2026.

Before kicking off its winter season, the 2021-built vessel operated a trans-Atlantic crossing that started in Civitavecchia, Italy.

The 14-night repositioning voyage included visits to destinations in Spain and Portugal.

Odyssey’s New York season starts with a series of seven-night cruises to the Bahamas and Florida, which sail to Nassau and Port Canaveral.

The itineraries are also highlighted by visits to Royal Caribbean’s private island destination of Perfect Day at CocoCay.

In a recent development, starting in January, the vessel will also offer longer cruises to the Eastern Caribbean, operating 11- and 12-night cruises to ports of call that include Bridgetown in Barbados, Charlotte Amalie in St. Thomas and St. John’s in Antigua.

The season runs through late April, when the Odyssey of the Seas is scheduled to embark on a repositioning voyage back to Europe.

Sailing from Cape Liberty to Civitavecchia, the 14-night cruise will feature visits to destinations in Portugal, Spain and Italy, including Ponta Delgada, Málaga, Cartagena and La Spezia.

The ship is scheduled to embark on another summer season in the Mediterranean in early November, offering weeklong cruises to the Greek Islands and Italy.

Completing five years of service in 2026, the Odyssey of the Seas underwent a routine drydock before its summer season.

The 4,200-passenger vessel underwent technical maintenance during the shipyard stay, in addition to overall upkeep work on public areas and staterooms.

Built at the Meyer Werft shipyard in Papenburg, Germany, the ship is part of Royal Caribbean’s Quantum-class series.

Scientists Studied Thousands of Ancient Skeletons and Found a Strange Truth About Human Progress

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It does a body good” slogan has some historical backing, at least in Europe.
  • “When children and adolescents have access to sufficient, high-quality food, they grow taller, within the constraints of genetic factors,” Manon Stephan, an economic historian at Germany’s University of Tübingen, said in a statement.
  • To test that idea, Stephan and colleagues at Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology examined 18,457 bones from 783 sites in 45 countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The dairy industry’s “Milk. It does a body good” slogan has some historical backing, at least in Europe. That’s one of the more surprising takeaways from a large study that used ancient skeletons to track how well people lived across Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 years. The researchers based their analysis on one telling measurement: human height.

“When children and adolescents have access to sufficient, high-quality food, they grow taller, within the constraints of genetic factors,” Manon Stephan, an economic historian at Germany’s University of Tübingen, said in a statement. “Therefore, height enables us to draw conclusions about living standards.”.

To test that idea, Stephan and colleagues at Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology examined 18,457 bones from 783 sites in 45 countries. In the study, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the team estimated people’s heights from their long bones. They then tracked how average height changed in each region and compared those changes with shifts in population density and technology.

In China, men were taller 7,000 years ago, averaging 5 feet 10 inches. Over time, however, their height steadily declined, reaching a low of just 5 feet 3 inches on average in the 19th century. Chinese women’s height also declined, though less drastically, falling from an average of 5 feet 2 inches 7,000 years ago to 4 feet 10 inches in more recent times.

According to recent reports, trends like these would be nearly impossible to trace through written records alone. “In many parts of the world, any written sources that would allow us to draw conclusions about economic development appear quite late on our timeline and are patchy in their distribution,” Stephan mentioned. “That’s why we rely on bones.” The bones in question came from 22 Asian and 23 European countries and were taken from the graves of commoners in both densely populated and rural regions.

In Europe, by contrast, the trends went in a different direction. Around 5,000 years ago, men in northern Europe averaged just 5 feet 4 inches. However, the study authors wrote, as pastoralist peoples migrated from the steppes of Eastern Europe and western Siberia, they brought with them more advanced dairy farming and the genetic trait of lactose tolerance. This led to greater consumption of dairy products, which the study identifies as a leading factor in increased height. Average heights in northern Europe continued to climb into the early Middle Ages, but sometime between 500 and 1000 C.E., they began to decline, a trend that lasted until the end of the 19th century.

Women’s heights followed a similar pattern. China and Japan experienced the steepest declines, while Europe saw a rise, though a less steep one than among men.

The authors wrote that “human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health.” Reconstructing this indicator offers insight into which societies provided better health and nutrition to their people. Surprisingly, technological progress did not prove to be a major factor in improving either.

According to recent reports, “Our study also confirmed that technological progress does not automatically lead to greater height,” remarked Jörg Baten, a professor of economic history at the University of Tübingen. “In China, for example, fresh, higher-yielding rice varieties and other innovations were introduced in the 11th century [C.E.]. While the higher yields enabled the empire to remain the dominant power, they did not subsequently lead to a better standard of living for the general population. Instead, population density increased: People had more children because this was seen as a form of security in old age. This meant, however, that each individual had not more to eat, but less. And importantly the quality declined, for example, in terms of high-quality protein.”.

It has been revealed that europe’s findings on technology mirrored Asia’s. Improved technology helped support denser populations, but it didn’t increase average height or necessarily improve the nutritional value of food.

According to recent reports, going forward, the authors hope to link more of these changes in height to shifts in social conditions or developments in agriculture. “This requires further research,” noted Mark Hudson, an archaeologist at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology. “However, the statistical data reveal trends and provide clues as to when these changes occurred.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Just like Wi-Fi-enabled lights and plugs and locks, smart thermostats give you the ability to automate an element of your home for increased convenience.
  • Using a companion app on your phone, you get intuitive and nuanced controls, including the ability to customize temperature schedules remotely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Just like Wi-Fi-enabled lights and plugs and locks, smart thermostats give you the ability to automate an element of your home for increased convenience. In this case, it’s your temperature controls. These devices tend to be a bit pricier than conventional thermostats, but it’s an upgrade that can pay for itself over time thanks to increased energy efficiency.

Using a companion app on your phone, you get intuitive and nuanced controls, including the ability to customize temperature schedules remotely. That comes in handy when, let’s say, you want to warm up the house earlier than usual if you head home from work early. You’re also able to track your usage with monthly energy reports, which can help you bring down your bills.

According to recent reports, for the past few months, my colleagues and I have been steadily testing smart thermostats throughout in our homes, including models from Google Nest, ecobee, and Honeywell Home. These are the models we tried, plus a few more we recommend based on our research and reviews. We’ve also included some expert advice on what to consider before you buy.

The ecobee covers the standard lineup of smart thermostat features, with climate control and money-saving that are commonplace among any of the top options, but sets itself apart with a wider range of smart features.

It doubles as a security base for your home security, serving as the arming and disarming mechanism. It also features a built-in air quality monitor that alerts you to poor air quality and sends reminders when you need to replace air filters in your furnace.

In a recent development, the ecobee comes with a separate smart sensor for precision control, allowing it to fine-tune the temperature in the rooms where you spend the most time. Though it comes with a single sensor, you can purchase more to add that precision throughout the house.

It also provides free Eco+ Software which works on your smartphone and generates energy reports that further maximize your energy savings.

Sources indicate that the smart thermostat also comes with a host of standard smart features. After connecting to a Google assistant or Alexa, the smart speaker built directly on the thermostat itself can take voice commands and even play music. It also comes with a three-year warranty from date of purchase.

Each purchase comes with a full converter kit as well, so if you aren’t presently in a home with a C-Wire, you can add one by following the kit instructions.

It has been revealed that for a smart thermostat that better fits a tight budget, Amazon has its own option that comes with many of the same energy-saving features at a lower overall price tag. Through the connected app, the thermostat tracks and reports your energy usage and peak time periods throughout the week and month.

It has been revealed that through Alexa, you can also set home, away, and sleep temperatures that you can schedule throughout the day and week in order to further maximize savings on your energy bill and optimize your air conditioning to your exact schedule. You can also set the temperature remotely from your phone through the Alexa app.

Beyond the controls, by using an Amazon product, the company will pass along potential rebate and saving opportunities that you could take advantage of by owning a smart thermostat.

As for upfront costs, the device is designed specifically for easy DIY installation so there is no need to hire an HVAC technician unless you want one.

The Honeywell T9 is a great choice if your primary concern is reducing energy use and lowering your bills. You need to pair it with one of Honeywell’s smart room sensors to take advantage of the thermostat’s full functionality, which is an extra hurdle, but the sensor only costs about $30, so it’s a short one.

One of the key ways the T9 saves money is through virtual fencing. Using your phone’s GPS, the thermostat automatically switches between home and away mode as you come and go. So, when you leave your house, energy usage is reduced across the board.

Honeywell also provides monthly usage reports that point out areas where energy can be reduced for a lower upfront cost. Adding more room sensors can increase the accuracy of those reports, giving you more chances to optimize your heating and cooling system.

The Honeywell T9 doesn’t have the same wide spectrum of features as our other recommendations, but it’s core functionality is very solid.

The newest generation of the Google Nest Thermostat has impressed our team as an easy-to-install, easy-to-use option that reduces energy use and is compatible with most HVAC systems. Like previous models, the smart thermostat builds a schedule, learns your temperature preferences, and reduces energy when it isn’t needed.

Reviews Editor Danny Perez installed the Nest in his own home and absolutely fell in the love with nearly every aspect of it. “To say I like this thermostat is an understatement: It lights up when I pass by to show me the interior temps, as well as local weather and humidity (it’s nice to know my presence is acknowledged, not gonna lie),” writes Perez.

Beyond the basic features, Perez also pointed out how much he likes the actual display and design of the thermostat. “Sure, other thermostats and window a/c units have similar smart features, but they don’t blend into my home the way the Google Nest thermostat does. I genuinely enjoy looking at it. I light up when I pass by it.”.

Read Full Nest Thermostat Review.

In a recent development, with a large, responsive touch screen, this basic Honeywell thermostat is easy to see from across the room, thanks to a large, custom-color display. It’s a versatile option, compatible with multiple smart home assistants. Like other models, it’s Energy Star-certified, which means that using one can help you save even more money through local rebates.

While the smart thermostat is great for easy scheduling and reading, it lacks the learning software of the Google Nest or the virtual fencing adjustments that many other smart thermostats have. That stated, it’s also considerably cheaper.

Sources indicate that most smart thermostats aren’t compatible with baseboard heating and cooling systems. This Mysa unit is the rare exception, and designed specifically to work with electric baseboards. Combine that with compatibility across every major smart home system, and the Mysa becomes one of very few thermostats with such capabilities.

It has been revealed that while the compatibility alone makes this a tempting choice, it also has many of the same high-end smart features as the competition. This includes virtual fencing, so when you head out for the day, the thermostat automatically reduces energy use.

Another key feature is its temperature monitor. Unlike many other devices, which only provide you with degrees, the Mysa smart thermostat also measures and reports humidity levels.

According to recent reports, traditional thermostats only require power through the four classic wires while smart thermostats typically require low- voltage power all day in order to run the display screen and some basic functions. This low-voltage power comes from an additional fifth wire called the “common” wire or C-Wire. The biggest potential matter you may have with installation is if your home lacks this wire.

If this is the case, it’s probably time to step away from your weekend home project and call an HVAC technician. While installing a common wire isn’t an incredibly difficult undertaking if you’re somewhat handy, it’s one that likely requires the expertise of a trained professional.

Some smart thermostats include installation kits that provide equipment and step-by-step instructions for adding a C-Wire to your current wiring. This can be a helpful addition to the handier among us, and may circumvent the need for an HVAC technician entirely, though you may want to keep one waiting in the wings if anything goes wrong.

Sources indicate that once you've wired and installed your smart thermostat, you can connect it to other devices in your home via Wi-Fi or occasionally Z-Wave. Most units are compatible with many major smart home ecosystems. While they’re compatible with many systems, I would still take a moment to check and make sure that a thermostat works specifically with the smart home setup you use at home.

Along with scheduling heating or cooling programs from the convenience of your phone, there are a handful of features that set smart thermostats apart from their traditional counterparts. Most smart models automatically adjust the temperature based on peak usage and some automatically respond to outdoor temperatures and set ideal temperatures indoors.

Sources indicate that other models use geofencing, or virtual fencing technology. This creates a radius around your home and detects how close or far away your smartphone is from it. With this, the smart thermostat eases energy use when you aren’t home, and ramps back up as you reenter the virtual boundary.

Several smart thermostats we cover use external sensors to expand the reach of temperature readings. Setup is typically no more complicated than placing the sensors around the house and syncing them up with the rest of the system.

They’re great for maintaining different temperatures in rooms, like keeping bedrooms and bathrooms warm and offices and laundry rooms cool. More precise temperature control also increases the potential for saving energy. Smart thermostats that include sensors as part of their systems often come with one, though some models require purchasing sensors separately.

It has been revealed that the Popular Mechanics Gear Team has tested several of these recommendations over the course of several months, including the ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium and the Google Nest Learning Thermostat. We installed these smart thermostats in our homes, set them up, and used them to keep ourselves warm and cool, as the seasons demanded. We gave them our seal of approval based on ease-of-use, installation process, programmable features, and how well the devices integrated with our smart home assistants, mobile devices, and tablets.

Recent findings suggest that A few thermostats, such as the Honeywell Home Smart Color Thermostat, made the list despite the fact that we haven’t tested them yet. In those cases, we picked options from established brands with the specs and features that are comparable to our tested recommendations, and have received strong reviews from customers at online retailers.

According to recent reports, we also prioritized options that were highly compatible with other smart devices and offered convenient features for everyday use. Price rice was a major consideration, as well: We chose models ranging from roughly $160 to $250, ensuring that we recommend a range of options that fit every need and budget.

Republicans tap Moreno and Jack to lead Senate and House campaign arms

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle.
  • It has been revealed that house and Senate Republicans picked their new campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen.
  • In their upcoming positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

It has been revealed that house and Senate Republicans picked their new campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack with leading the GOP campaign arms for the 2028 election cycle.

In their upcoming positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.

Republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections. In the Senate, South Dakota’s John Thune was reelected Republican leader without any opposition, while Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise in a closed-door, secret-ballot election to lead House Republicans next year.

Moreno will succeed South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

“Republicans must enter this next election clear-eyed: the road ahead back to a Republican Senate majority will by no means be easy but the fight has never been so key,” the Ohio senator remarked in a statement.

Speaking to reporters on Capitol Hill, Moreno described his fresh role as “a hell of a job.” He said Republicans would be “absolute savages” on ending government corruption and continuing “to work for the American people.”.

“I suspect the best tailwind we’ll have is that the Democrats will learn all the wrong lessons,” he told reporters.

Industry observers note that moreno, a close ally of President Donald Trump, is currently serving his first term. He first ran for Senate during the 2022 cycle but dropped out of a crowded GOP primary eventually won by JD Vance. Two years later, buoyed by an endorsement from Trump, he won a contested primary for the state’s other Senate seat and went on to oust Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown that fall.

Brown is poised to return to the Senate after defeating appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week in a special election for the remaining Senate term of Vice President Vance. While Ohio has swung heavily toward Republicans over the past decade, Democrats scored big wins in the Buckeye State last week, winning several statewide offices and flipping three seats in the U.S. House.

But assuming he runs again for a full term, Brown will be on the ballot in 2028, setting up what’s likely to be a tense home-state fight.

Recent findings suggest that in an apparent reference to the returning Brown, Moreno offered some Washington advice Tuesday: “Make sure you rent. Do not buy.”.

The 2028 Senate map gives Republican pickup opportunities in a handful of swing states, including Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Upcoming Hampshire and Pennsylvania. The party will also be defending battleground seats in Alaska, Iowa, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Also on the Senate ballot are races for Republican-held seats in Kansas and South Carolina, where Democrats scored surprise wins last week.

Industry observers note that on the House side, Jack defeated Indiana Rep. Rudy Yakym III to become the next chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee. He takes office after one of the worst elections for the GOP in recent decades and will succeed outgoing NRCC Chair Richard Hudson, who lost his own North Carolina seat last week.

House Republicans face the tough task of cutting into Democrats’ 40-plus-seat majority next cycle. But the party will have a slew of pickup opportunities, given the sheer number of seats Democrats won in historically red territory this year.

Industry observers note that like Moreno, Jack was first elected to Congress 2024, leveraging a close relationship with Trump to win an open seat outside Atlanta. He previously was White House director of political affairs during Trump’s first term and was a senior adviser to the president’s 2024 campaign. Over the past two years, he served as the NRCC’s recruitment chair.

Savannah Behrmann contributed to this report.

The 8 Best Home Generators Are a Big Investment. These Deliver Reliable Power During an Outage.

📅 07 Nov 2018 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Recent findings suggest that stronger and more frequent severe weather events are making a compelling argument for investing in a home generator.
  • The term “home generator” can be confusing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that stronger and more frequent severe weather events are making a compelling argument for investing in a home generator. A large portable generator or a permanently installed standby generator can keep your entire home powered and operational for several days, or at least keep a few critical appliances such as a refrigerator running until the power comes back on. The cost of emergency power is never a small investment, though it is an increasingly key one.

The term “home generator” can be confusing. It’s an unofficial category that includes larger portable generators capable of powering several appliances or a few critical circuits using a transfer switch (not all portable generators are built for this task). It also includes permanently installed standby generators that can automatically switch to whole-home backup power when the lights go out. Choosing the right size generator primarily comes down to how much power you think you’ll need in an emergency.

Sources indicate that there are many reliable home generators that deliver a great deal of power. Some offer you the choice of running on multiple different fuels, while other models use an inverter that can give you quieter and “cleaner” operation. There is a nice range of prices available, too, so you can easily find a generator below that fits your needs as well as your budget.

For the generators on this list that we tested, we considered the difficulty of unboxing, assembling, and starting each generator for the first time, because few things are as frustrating as buying a tool that turns out to be unnecessarily complicated from the get-go.

Industry observers note that once set up, the generators we reviewed were subjected to different load conditions, including things such as power tools, home appliances, and even recharging large power stations. We assessed the features that distinguish these generators from each other, including safety features, app connectivity, and portability, among other things.

A few picks on our list have not been tested, but we included them here after considerable research, taking into account the brand’s reputation, our knowledge of its product lines, various outside reviews, and our own experience testing similar models from those same brands.

The DuroMax XP11000iH is a powerful midsize dual-fuel inverter generator, capable of keeping most homes up and running for an extended period of time. Inverter generators are a step above traditional generators because they convert alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC) and then back again to AC. This process creates cleaner, more efficient power and enables the generator to run more quietly and fuel efficiently.

Having two fuel options—gas and propane—provides a significant boost of convenience by allowing you to use whatever’s handy. No gasoline? You can use the same tank of propane you use for your gas grill. It’s also parallel-capable, so you can daisy-chain it with another generator if you need extra power.

According to recent reports, the generator is enclosed in a large, sturdy plastic casing, which makes it durable and provides a fair amount of sound dampening. Of the many gas generators I’ve tested, it may be the quietest model that’s capable of backing up a whole home, especially when it’s running on propane, which trims it down by another few decibels. At 61 decibels on a 20 percent load, it’s about as loud as a dishwasher. Most comparably sized generators go up to around 80 decibels—about the same volume as a police siren.

According to recent reports, in addition to a full suite of essential modern safety features such as a carbon monoxide shutoff and low-oil shutoff, it goes the extra mile with lots of little touches, like remote start. The integrated battery tender keeps it ready to start, no matter how long it’s been sitting, which can be a lifesaver, too. When you do run out to check it, an onboard display shows you key stats such as hours run, current load, and voltage output.

Sources indicate that the only downside I could find was its weight. At upward of 200 pounds, it isn’t easy to carry. It does have wheels and sturdy handles, though, so it isn’t hard to wheel around on flat, paved ground—if you can push a loaded wheelbarrow, you can push this. Not that you’ll need to move it much; it’s a very sturdy generator, and it comes assembled with the wheels and handles attached (not all generators come with those pre-attached). —Reviewed by Nick Hilden.

Technically, there are cheaper generators out there, but the Generac GP9500E offers an outstanding blend of capability, quality, and durability at a very reasonable price. As such, this is where I’d steer you if you’re trying to shave down your spend.

Its 9,500-watt running capacity is slightly higher than the DuroMax’s, and it’s capable of powering all but the largest of homes. It can get a little noisy under a heavy load, but that’s common with units this size. It let out a relatively moderate purr when it was just powering the lights and a few appliances, but it became more of a roar when the heat kicked on.

With three fuel options—gas, propane, and natural gas—you get about as much versatility as you could possibly expect from a generator. A relatively large 7.5-gallon gas tank delivers a long runtime between fill-ups. And, while I was initially skeptical as to the necessity of the third fuel option, having natural gas support indicated its value when a storm knocked out the power, and I didn’t have gas or propane on hand. All I needed to do was plug it into the natural gas line, and suddenly my house was the only one on the block with lights on.

Beyond that, though, it’s a fairly basic model. It has essential safety features such as low-oil and CO shutdown, but lacks elements such as a fancy digital display, remote start, or app. I don’t necessarily think that’s a problem: It can be helpful to get a piece of machinery that doesn’t go overboard with features. Its control panel is about as straightforward as can be, and it’s a cinch to get up and running.

Like my top pick, the GP9500E is exceedingly heavy. It’s also quite sturdy, though, which feels like a fair trade. The outlet covers aren’t as flimsy and breakable as with many other models of a similar price point. It isn’t completely immobile: It has wheels and handles that make it easy to cart around short distances. Realistically, though, weight is almost always going to be an problem with any generator capable of backing up your house.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, its selling point is the price. It’s hard to find a quality tri-fuel generator for around $1,100, and the GP9500E performs well if you don’t mind losing out on some bells and whistles.

Sources indicate that when AC power isn’t available, the greenest way to recharge a power station is with solar panels. However, the panel’s maximum power output often exceeds the maximum solar input, so they just can’t recharge fast enough. In these cases, whole-home, battery-based backup systems need the help of a fuel-based generator to recharge, so you’re not left high and dry if the power’s still out. That’s where the EcoFlow Smart Generator 4000 comes in.

This dual-fuel (gas or propane) generator connects to select EcoFlow power stations via a DC charging and communication cable, including the Delta Pro, Delta Pro 3, Delta 3, Delta 3 Plus, and Delta 2 Max. (Note: If your preferred brand is Anker, it also makes a fuel generator that’s compatible with some of its power stations, the 5500 Tri-Fuel Inverter Generator, which we also tested and reviewed.) This DC connection allows autonomous operation, so when a station’s battery hits critically low levels, the generator automatically starts to recharge it.

Industry observers note that you can also recharge non-DC-compatible power stations by simply plugging them into the AC output, though it’s a slower recharge. If it’s an EcoFlow station, you can still automate startup, too, by pairing over Bluetooth. But you won’t be able to do this with other brands of power stations.

Industry observers note that our test editor Bradley Ford noted that EcoFlow’s app is one of the best features of this generator. Connecting over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, he used it to monitor fuel consumption and output, as well as set automated functions. He also tested how it can set the charging speed, monitor power output, and schedule times to start and stop the generator. He especially liked that the app provides a lot of useful information as well, such as generator fuel usage and estimated runtime.

Of course, it can work as a standalone generator, too, though there are some limitations. Ford notes that there are only two outlets: a 120-volt, 20-amp outlet and a 120-volt, 30-amp outlet. The latter outlet can connect to a manual transfer switch installed in your home, but it won’t be able to power any 240-volt circuits, and the total output of 3,200 watts is only enough to power a few circuits. However, he thinks it would work well for RV use, and because it’s an inverter generator, it’s better at safely powering sensitive electronics like TVs and computers. — Reviewed by Bradley Ford.

Full EcoFlow Dual-Fuel Smart Generator 4000 Review.

Whether you’re connecting devices individually, powering an RV, or running home backup power during a storm, this generator from Westinghouse (model WGen9500DF) covers all the bases. In addition to being dual-fuel (gas or propane), it includes both 30- and 50-amp outputs capable of powering 120- and 240-volt circuits. That means you could connect this generator to a transfer switch installed in your home using either option. And with 9,500 running watts of power, it’s enough for several critical circuits in your home, including the ones that run on 240 volts, such as a heating/ventilation/air-conditioning system, electric dryer, or well pump.

It has been revealed that several other features caught our attention, including a push-button electric start and stop (no need to mess with a pull cable), plus a remote start key fob. There’s an automatic low-oil shutoff, and the display provides the voltage output, frequency, and lifetime hours (this can run up to 12 hours on a 6.6-gallon tank of gasoline). The only drawback is the 74-decibel noise level. While that’s typical of generators of this type, if you're planning on using this to power an RV or camper, it may be too loud for some parks, as many limit generator noise to under 70 decibels.

It has been revealed that while it does not offer as much power as some of the choices on our list, Champion’s 4,750-watt generator has enough capacity to run three or four critical 120-volt circuits in your home during an outage. It will also power small to medium campers and RVs via a dedicated 30-amp, 120-volt RV receptacle. Listed at around $600, this generator gives you a lot for the price you pay.

Sources indicate that this generator uses a 224-cc engine with a 4.7-gallon fuel tank, enabling it to run for up to 14 hours (up to 10 hours using propane). A gauge displays a readout of the runtime hours and voltage output, and there’s an automated shutoff feature if the oil starts to run low. Since it’s dual-fuel, this generator can run off propane in addition to gasoline. For instance, if you are using it with an RV, you can run it off a camper’s propane tank without having to pack and haul a gas can. Likewise, with the included adapter hose, you can hook it up to a 20-pound propane tank.

In a recent development, there are a few drawbacks. Beyond the somewhat low wattage output for whole-home backup, there are no 240-volt outlets, so if you need that many volts to power circuits in your home for something such as a dryer or water heater, this model won’t be right for you. But if you just need something to keep some lights on and run a few appliances, this generator will get the job done and not cost you a ton of money up front to do it. — Reviewed by Bradley Ford.

Sources indicate that there are many reasons to opt for an inverter generator, but the two biggest ones are: cleaner, more stable power (important for powering electronics safely) and less noise. Loudness becomes a major factor with larger generators, as more power requires a more powerful engine. That’s why we were so impressed with this model (EU7000iS) from Honda. It delivers a lot of power but at notably low loudness levels.

It’s important to note that this is not a small generator. It weighs in at 263 pounds, making it one of the heaviest on our list. That mentioned, we found it fairly comfortable to move around. The metal frame that houses the generator has a folding handle that locks into place and is capped with soft grips, while on the front of the frame there are strong 10-inch rubber wheels. This made it fairly easy to roll around, even up some gradual slopes.

In a recent development, it’s also quite sturdy. The outer casing is constructed of stamped metal and impact-resistant composite hard plastic, with two large, hinged maintenance doors that lock into place.

According to recent reports, once we fired up the generator, it was noticeably quieter than other models we’ve tested, even when outputting a 60 percent load. Using an app-based sound meter, we were reading around 70 decibels from 15 feet away, which is lower than you would see with a non-inverter generator. This is helped by an “Eco Throttle” mode that adjusts the engine speed to meet demand as different devices are added, but we found even the standard throttle mode was fairly quiet as well.

Other things we liked were an app that allows for remote operation over Bluetooth, ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection, a carbon monoxide (CO) sensor, and 240-volt output over a 30-amp connection, which will let the generator connect to a manual transfer switch for sending direct power to your home electrical box.

The two downsides are the cost (it’s very expensive at more than $4,000) and the fact that it can only be powered by gasoline; Honda doesn’t offer dual- or tri-fuel models for using propane or natural gas. But if those two considerations don’t bother you, the EU7000iS Inverter Generator is a high-quality machine that will keep you more quietly powered than some of the competition.

Full Honda EU7000iS 7000-Watt Inverter Generator Review.

Battery-based backup systems are getting smarter and more powerful every year, making them an increasingly strong contender to fuel-based standby generators. This model from EcoFlow is one of the most powerful we’ve tested.

It has been revealed that the power station combines a separate inverter unit with two 6-kilowatt-hour batteries for a total of 12-kilowatt-hour capacity. That’s enough to run power-hungry devices simultaneously—things such as heating/ventilation/air-conditioning systems, electric ovens and dryers, microwaves, and air-conditioning units. Add to this increased solar input, and you can recharge faster, too. For our tests, we connected this to a home electrical system in the home using EcoFlow’s Smart Home Panel 3, which acts as the automatic transfer switch.

During testing, our reviewer experienced two power outages, one for a few seconds and one for several minutes. This power station features an Emergency Power Supply (EPS) mode, which facilitates a 20-millisecond switch to backup power—without this set, it normally switches in about five seconds. During the longer outage, the switch from grid to backup power, and then back again, was seamless. It was fast enough that the lights never flickered and the internet never dropped.

In a recent development, several advanced smart features stand out. The smartphone app enables you to view power usage, down to the circuit, preset what circuits get backup power during outages, manually turn circuits on and off, and schedule automated tasks such as charging and discharging. You’ll also receive notifications when the grid goes down and the backup power takes over. If you live in an area where electricity is cheaper during low-peak hours, it can also prioritize recharging from grid power by choosing those times of day.

Meanwhile, this system is highly expandable. You can add up to eight more batteries for a total of 10, and an inlet box that comes with the smart panel has three ports. You could plug a Delta Pro Ultra X, bolstered by extra batteries, into each port to increase the total energy storage up to a whopping 184.3 kilowatt-hours of capacity and 36 kilowatts of continuous output.

One of the biggest things our reviewer appreciates about the Delta Pro Ultra X and Smart Home Panel 3 is the peace of mind it gives. If the grid goes down, they know that their home systems will continue to run. — Reviewed by Bradley Ford.

In a recent development, pulsar is a relatively fresh brand in the generator business and doesn’t have a long track record. We first spotted it on Amazon and didn’t seriously consider its generators for testing. That was, up until our test editor needed a generator (with specific features and on a budget) after a generator failed at his solar-powered off-grid cabin. Happily, the Pulsar 7,250-Watt Dual-Fuel Inverter Generator showed up quickly and didn’t disappoint.

It has been revealed that the generator was easy to assemble and prep, taking only 15 minutes. After adding oil, it was connected to a propane cylinder and was up and running on the first cycle of the starter. Our first task was to charge a solar battery bank during a wintertime period when there was not enough available sunlight, and it worked perfectly.

We have logged more than 20 hours of use so far, running it primarily on propane connected to a 100-pound cylinder (enough fuel to last a couple of months). This Pulsar puts out very clean power, with a claimed total harmonic distortion (THD) of less than 3 percent, which met the requirements of the solar inverter-charger I was using. Using the inverter to monitor the current frequency, we found that it was indeed very stable with minimal variance, between 59.97 and 60.09 Hz. All things considered, the Pulsar 7,250-Watt Dual-Fuel is a good value for the specs, capacity, and features. — Reviewed by Bradley Ford.

True whole-home backup requires a professionally installed standby generator like Generac’s 22-kilowatt home standby generator. It’s designed to power a house that’s roughly 2,500 square feet. If you need to run specialized medical devices, work from home, or have kids who are learning from home, this model is a sound investment.

Another benefit of this bundle is that it includes a transfer switch, which is required if you’re planning to install this type of generator. It supports 200-amp electrical service, providing the backup circuits needed to power high-voltage appliances such as refrigerators and well pumps, along with air conditioning and heating systems. Plus, there’s built-in WiFi for checking the status of your generator and receiving maintenance alerts when you’re not at home.

Sources indicate that you could just drive over to your local hardware store and buy a large portable generator to use as a home backup, but we wouldn’t recommend it. You want to make sure you’re getting a generator that can back up your home and power all the appliances, lights, and electronics inside. (Plus some extra watts in case you need them down the line.).

In addition, there are often state and local laws or homeowners association rules and restrictions around using them in residential neighborhoods. Choosing poorly or setting up your backup generator incorrectly could damage the generator or short out your house power at best, or lead to fire, electrocution, or carbon monoxide poisoning at worst.

Picking the best generator for your home starts with a little math. Ideally, you want to calculate how much energy you need to keep your house running, and buy a generator that can handle everything you want to power in an emergency, with room to spare.

Industry observers note that the two key specs to pay attention to are the running wattage and starting wattage (e.g., 9,500 running watts / 12,500 starting watts). Running wattage is effectively your generator’s capacity: It tells you how much power a generator can produce steadily without any possibility of an overload. Starting wattage is the generator’s max output, or how much power it can produce for short, peak bursts when appliances first switch on.

When you are making your list, note what items are 120-volt and which ones are 240-volt appliances. It’s not hard to identify them. Refrigerators, small appliances, and most electronics run on 120-volt power and plug into standard outlets. Anything that requires 240 volts—electric dryers, well pumps, and HVAC systems—is either hardwired into your electrical system or has a dedicated 240-volt outlet. If you need to power the latter, the installation of a transfer switch and a generator that outputs at least 30 amps/240 volts may be required.

If you’re just looking to keep the fridge, lights, and a few modest appliances going through a short blackout, you can usually get away with a generator that supplies 3,000 to 5,000 watts. If you want to run the heat, hot water, and several appliances at once, initiative on using at least 6,000 to 8,000 watts. If you think you’re going to be adding large appliances such as laundry machines and dishwashers, expect to need 10,000 watts or more.

A piece of advice we have: Once you figure out how much you need, opt for buying a generator that outputs around 20 percent more than that. It’s not uncommon to realize you need more than you thought you would.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also crucial to consider that, while generators are certainly a hefty investment, they usually stand the test of time. Consumer-grade portable generators can run anywhere from 1,000 to 3,000 hours, sometimes more. If you run one for 100 hours per year, it should last for 10 to 30 years.

There are four basic types of generators, each with advantages and disadvantages.

Industry observers note that the most traditional of the generator category, these run on carbon-based fuels like gasoline, propane, and natural gas. Some allow you to switch between them. Dual-fuel models add the option of either propane or natural gas, while tri-fuel versions offer all three fuel options. These generators can be small, offering as little as 1,000 watts of power output, or run very large, as much as 20,000 watts or more.

According to recent reports, different fuels offer different power capabilities. For example, a tri-fuel generator may offer 9,500 running watts and 12,500 starting watts with gasoline, but only 8,500/11,200 with propane and 7,500/9,500 with natural gas. Regardless of the fuel you choose, this type of generator must always be operated 5 to 20 feet away from the home or any window or door, because the carbon monoxide exhaust is deadly. Even a garage with an open door is not safe.

Often this type of generator is called portable, but that's a relative term: Almost all of them weigh more than 100 pounds, and many are upwards of 200. Many are on wheels, making them relatively easy to store in a garage and wheel outside when you need them, but actually moving one will likely require at least two people.

Inverter generators look and operate the same as other portable generators, but have an added component–a power inverter– that converts the alternating current (AC) power generated by its fuel source to DC (Direct Current), then inverts it back to AC before putting it out.

Generators without an inverter generate varying degrees of distortion in the sine wave of the alternating current, which can trigger power surges and other complications in some electronics. The inverter stabilizes the power, almost like a filter, “cleaning” it for more sensitive electronics like TVs and laptops.

Sources indicate that so why doesn’t every generator have an inverter? Inverters are expensive, so the generators are, too.

Realistically speaking, you don’t need an inverter generator to power major appliances and your house power, but if you’re running a full home backup (or if you count a TV or laptop among your essential electronics), holding out for an inverter is a smart move.

In a recent development, while often referred to as “solar generators” because they can be paired with solar panels, power stations are not really true generators. They're advanced battery banks that store power, which you precharge using AC power or solar panels. They can’t generate electricity in real time.

According to recent reports, but because they can offer many of the same electrical outputs as a fuel generator, they can function similarly to a traditional generator for as long as the batteries retain a charge. Some stations are very small and meant only for off-grid adventures like camping trips, but some are large enough to run whole-home systems that can produce 14,400 watts or more with expandable batteries.

Since power stations don't run on fuel or have an engine, they can be used indoors without the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning and operate with almost no noise.

The downside is that once the power is depleted, the power station must be recharged. If the power grid is still unavailable, it can take many hours in ideal sunny conditions if all you have are solar panels. You can use a traditional generator to recharge a power station, but some may view that as defeating the purpose.

It has been revealed that standby generators are permanently installed generators designed to automatically take over for your house power in the event of an outage. You can set them to power your whole house, or only specific circuits, giving you precise control. Standby generators start at around 10,000 watts (10 kilowatts) but can go up to much higher. For the average home, a range of 10 to 25 kilowatts is usually enough.

They typically require professional installation, making them the most costly option. Since many large portable generators can effectively back up a house for a few hours for a lot less money, standby models are still considered a more niche option.

When you draw too much power from your generator, its performance will start to decline. At home, your lights will start to dim or flicker, and appliances may turn off momentarily. The generator itself may also start to get louder, or sound like it’s working extra hard to keep up.

If you notice these signs, start turning off and unplugging non-essential power sources immediately, or turn the generator off entirely for ten minutes or so to reduce the power load.

Industry observers note that this is an urgent problem, so do not wait to take action: If you overwork your generator for too long, it’s only a matter of time before it starts to overheat, produce smoke, or break down. The damage from an extended overload could permanently damage the generator or, worse, start a fire.

With the right size for your home, a portable or standby generator can run as long as you keep feeding it fuel and stay within its running wattage capacity; however, you should not run them indefinitely. Manufacturers recommend you allow them to rest for 30 minutes or more after at least 24 hours of use. Check the manual of your generator for its specific recommendations.

You will get more time from each tank of gas if you draw less power, so it helps to pay extra attention to your electricity usage when you’re running the generator.

Sources indicate that make sure to turn your gas and/or propane generators off when it’s time to refill the tank. Failing to do so could lead to a fire.

Power stations, since they rely on electricity or solar power, can almost always be charged while in use.

Industry observers note that never run a fuel-based generator (gasoline, propane, natural gas) indoors. Burning fuel releases carbon monoxide (CO), which will quickly build up to deadly levels in an enclosed space.

In a recent development, set your generator up outside, between 5 and 20 feet away from your home and/or any garages, sheds, or other walls. Position it as far as possible from doors, windows, and vents, with the exhaust positioned away from the house, to minimize the possibility of fumes wafting in. If you keep it outside all year round, find a naturally covered position where snow won’t naturally pile up around it.

My generator is situated near my home’s power box, which is located on a windowless side of my home. It stands about five feet from the exterior wall, with plenty of space on all sides, but close enough to sit under the roof peak overhang 20 feet above.

David is a Reviews Editor for Hearst’s Enthusiast Group, contributing to Popular Mechanics, Runner’s World, Bicycling, Best Products, and Biography. He has over 25 years of experience writing about and reviewing consumer electronics, kitchen appliances, DIY products, outdoor gear, and more. He also spent years covering the ever-changing world of online retail. To relax, he loves experimenting with new recipes, tweaking his smart home setup, and spending time outdoors on his bike or camping.

Breaking: Independents decide the election, again!
