Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Rain shower, private patio, indoor hammock, design-forward, walkable to beach.

In a recent development, in the mood for some island romance? There’s no better place for love than this gorgeous apartment with the sea in easy reach. With interiors curated by Dreamers Welcome, a Puerto Rico–based hospitality group focused on luxury stays with a laid-back vibe, you’ll also have exclusive access to amenities at nearby boutique hotel Dreamcatcher by DW. This includes a daily vegan or vegetarian breakfast, guided tours, yoga on the beach, and a gift store to shop at with crafts by local creatives. Back at the apartment, take in the views from the intimate patio space, sway on the indoor hammock, and fall into the ever-cozy sofa. With a double vanity and rich red polished shower, even a trip to the bathroom here will make you feel like you’re in a design magazine.

Neighborhood: SanturceThings to do nearby: Condado, Ocean Park, Old San Juan, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico, Miramar.

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, barbecue, outdoor seating area, beach access, kid-friendly amenities.

This sunny gem of an Airbnb makes group getaways look easy. Just steps from the Ocean Park beach—where you’re sure to see kitesurfers aplenty—you’ll also have a pool to lounge in and around right at home. In fact, the backyard is bigger than it first appears: There’s a separate barbecue area, as well as a swing chair and a canopy day bed for the best kind of outdoor nap. Located in a gated community, you’ll have privacy as well as peace and quiet, but not without easy access to the local hot spots that make San Juan the buzzy city that it is.

Industry observers note that each of the bedrooms has sweet design touches, from whimsy and bright colors to room-darkening shades and comfy linens. The fourth bedroom is located in a separate, more private space with its own bathroom, so it’s best for those who value more privacy, or the parents on a family vacation.

Neighborhood: SanturceThings to do nearby: Ocean Park Beach, Calle Loíza, Las Marias, Playa del Pueblo.

#134247. Trump says no Iran deal needed after conflict drove GOP’s midterm losses

Trump says no Iran deal needed after conflict drove GOP’s midterm losses

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a Wednesday ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery in honor of Veterans Day.
  • President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.
  • The possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a Wednesday ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery in honor of Veterans Day. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images).

President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.

The possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections. House Democrats will have more than 250 seats come January, and Senate Democrats will have at least 55 seats in the Senate — with Alaska’s competitive race still uncalled.

Polls leading up to Election Day and since have shown that a majority of voters, and a sizeable chunk of Trump’s Republican base, felt the Iran conflict was a mistake.

Industry observers note that vice President JD Vance penned a lengthy social media post the day after the election, blaming, in large part, the Iran war for the coast-to-coast Democratic victories. Some GOP lawmakers have also called for an end to the conflict, which drove up fuel and other commodity prices.

Industry observers note that "The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote the morning after the GOP wipeout. "The president himself remarked so last night.".

Sources indicate that trump has said that he agrees with Vance’s assessment but that if he had to decide again whether to join Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in striking Iranian targets, he would reach the same conclusion. On Monday, he told reporters that the Iran war "militarily is effectively over.".

Vance had been Trump’s designated top negotiator in the talks with Iran’s remaining leaders, but the president stated Thursday on social media that he had ordered his second-in-command to instead “focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.”.

Sources indicate that “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” he added. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!".

The situation along the Strait of Hormuz remains contested and dangerous for commercial vessels, including ones that deliver a large amount of the world’s oil products. Iranian officials contend that they control most of the key waterway.

Trump, Vance and other administration officials have remarked in recent weeks that they were open to continuing talks with Iran, while criticizing Tehran's negotiating tactics. Last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also is Trump’s national security adviser, told reporters that Iran's latest demands were unreasonable.

Sources indicate that trump’s announcement Thursday could represent his latest way to try assuaging GOP voters, including members of his “Make America Great Again” base. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after the midterms and released Tuesday revealed that a majority of Republicans (51 percent) want Congress to pass legislation that would end the Iran conflict. Overall, 71 percent of Americans would support such a bill, the survey found.

The conflict was front-and-center during the midterms campaign.

Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers, who lost the Senate race in Michigan to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, called for the Iran conflict to end "quickly.".

In a recent development, “Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life. Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down," Rogers said in one campaign ad.

On Capitol Hill, GOP lawmakers have tried giving Trump cover, while raising some concerns about high gas prices and questioning whether the president and his team have a viable exit strategy.

As the midterms campaign hit the homestretch in late September, two Iowa Republicans in tight races, Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks, voted with Democrats on a measure to end the conflict.

Recent findings suggest that “With the negotiating window closed, sustained combat operations now require congressional authorization,” Nunn, an Air Force veteran, wrote on social media. “I will not support another open-ended war.”.

Nunn and Miller-Meeks both lost their seats last week, despite breaking with the president over the war.

Trump’s declaration this week of a military end to the Iran war came more than seven years after he offered some foreshadowing during a June 25, 2019, exchange with this CQ Roll Call reporter in the Oval Office.

It has been revealed that asked that day what his exit strategy would be if war ever broke out with Iran, he stated: “You’re not going to need an exit strategy. I don’t do exit strategies.”.
